MBE-decorated trombonist Dennis Rollins spent eight years touring with Maceo Parker before forming this six-piece groove outfit. The band moves from heavyweight funk and swing to Latin-tinged rhythms, with Rollins' trombone always at centre stage.

A first-call drummer on the London scene, he has recorded and performed with Grammy-winner Kurt Elling and toured alongside Wynton Marsalis. His quartet draws on roots in Kansas Smitty's and Mark Kavuma's Banger Factory — two of the capital's most celebrated bands.
For more than 30 years, acclaimed alto saxophonist, composer and improviser Mar

London trumpeter Loz Speyer brings his Space Trio — drawn from his longstanding quintet Inner Space — to the Vortex downstairs bar, performing compositions by Ornette Coleman and Dave Holland alongside original music. The trio's set draws on material from Inner Space's Live in Leipzig, released in July 2024 on Spherical Records.

Guitarist and composer Jean de Talhouët leads this London sextet, celebrating the release of In Time and Spirit on Clonmell Social. Saxophonist George Crowley guests on the album's title suite, alongside a band whose sound draws on spiritual grooves, polyrhythms, and modal exploration.

London-born keys man and vocalist who co-wrote the gold-selling "Revival Song" from Gregory Porter's Grammy-nominated All Rise. A long-standing member of Laura Mvula's touring band, he appears as a featured vocalist on her Ivor Novello Award-winning Pink Noise.

Former members of Hi-Tension, Beggar & Co, Light of the World, and Incognito, this London supergroup has released three collective albums — Full Circle, Lifted, and Ancestral Voices — on the Expansion Records label. Their live set draws on a shared catalogue of Top 40 hits including "British Hustle," "Somebody Help Me Out," and "London Town."

A founder member of the London Django Collective, guitarist Harry Diplock arrived in London from Devon in 2012 originally as a builder of guitars. His latest album Swifts, released in May 2026, showcases his electric trio alongside Sol Grimshaw and Isaac Burland.

Rated by the London Evening Standard as "one of Britain's best singer-pianists," this British pianist-vocalist brings his trio to Soho, drawing on a catalogue that spans celebrated repertoire albums devoted to Hoagy Carmichael, Dudley Moore, and Stan Getz. He is also the author of the Rough Guides to The Beatles and Frank Sinatra.

artist_name: Colin Webster / Matthew Grigg / Caius Williams / Fabian Neubauer
Jazz Up the 80s with the Jay Rayner Sextet
description: Founded in 2012 as a quartet, the band expanded to a sextet in 2022. Fronted by MasterChef judge and pianist Jay Rayner, the six-piece deliver fresh arrangements of tracks by Sade, Matt Bianco, Everything But The Girl, Swing Out Sister, Sting and more.
Solo vocal tribute to Billie Holiday performed by Nina Kristofferson at PizzaExpress Live The Pheasantry, 8.00pm.

Led by Oreste 'Sambroso' Noda — who previously worked with Buena Vista Social Club singer Ibrahim Ferrer — this London-based seven-piece brings Cuba's golden era to Soho. Expect Cuban Son, Rumba, and a loving tribute to the music that defined that era.

Hitting No. 1 on the iTunes chart for the genre above Frank Sinatra and Ella Fitzgerald with his debut single 'Brazil', this British swing vocalist has also performed sell-out shows at 54 Below in New York City and now brings his big band to Soho for a night of Rat Pack classics and beyond.

A British-Polish singer-songwriter who released debut album Something Good Out of Nothing on Swift Half Records in 2025, Marzec returns to The Pheasantry after performing as lead singer and saxophonist alongside Pick Withers of Dire Straits — this time bringing The Neighbours for a full band show of soul-rooted originals.

A London-based five-piece with deep roots in the blues, they mix original compositions with covers drawing on the songbooks of Bill Withers, Freddie King, and Ray Charles. Their 2024 single Escape was released on Bluenoteman Records.

Founded in London in 2018, this brass collective blends pop and rock arrangements with original material drawn from influences spanning Ezra Collective to New Orleans bands like The Soul Rebels. Their latest release, Brass, Run! EP, dropped in July 2026.

Sonic Youth founding guitarist Thurston Moore pairs with improviser and cellist Mark Wastell for a rare free improvisation duo at the Vortex — Moore's post-punk noise heritage meeting Wastell's reductionist approach to sound.

Born in Islington, guitarist Ray Russell made his professional debut replacing Vic Flick as lead guitarist in the John Barry Seven. His session credits span an extraordinary range, including work with Gil Evans, Van Morrison, Tina Turner, Jack Bruce, and Bryan Ferry.
Romanian pianist who in 2015 became the first non-American to win the Grand Prix at the Jacksonville piano competition. He has shared a festival stage with Chick Corea and Gregory Porter.

Best known for his collaboration with Artful Dodger on the hit "Please Don't Turn Me On," his current project, Lifford Roots, sees him lead a full live band — a show that has already sold out London venues including Pizza Express Live and Soul Mama. Catch him at the 606 Club on 8 November to mark the occasion in style.
Mexican-born vibraphonist Patricia Brennan leads her Septet — one of the most original voices in contemporary improvised music.

UK saxophonist, vocalist and composer and the first Cheltenham musician to perform on the main festival stage, Kim Cypher brings her band to PizzaExpress Live Soho on 9 November. Her third album, Catching Moments, features guest performers Liane Carroll, Ray Gelato, Antonio Forcione and Ashley Slater.
High-voltage ensemble led by alto saxophonist David Binney, one of contemporary music's most prolific voices.

American pianist Larry Fuller — known for his work with Ernestine Anderson and the Jeff Hamilton Trio — brings his swinging mainstream approach to PizzaExpress, channelling the tradition of Oscar Peterson and Hank Jones.

Sheffield-based quartet Family Band — Kim Macari (trumpet), Riley Stone-Lonergan (tenor saxophone), Tom Rivière (bass) and Steve Hanley (drums) — met studying at Leeds College of Music in 2008. Their third album, released on Discus Music, is their most democratic yet, with all four members contributing compositions.

Trained by Nancy Marano of the Manhattan School of Music and launched in Italy at a major international music festival, this London-based vocalist brings two decades of experience to the Pheasantry. Her latest album Dreaming Life revisits and expands on the critically acclaimed Minor Moments (2019), her collaboration with composer Martin Pyne.

artist_name: The Wonder of Stevie – The Music of Stevie Wonder
description: Vocalist Noel McCalla — voted one of Britain's top soul singers by Blues and Soul Magazine — leads this six-piece alongside saxophonist Derek Nash, a member of Jools Holland's Rhythm and Blues Orchestra since 2004. The band's musicians have previously performed with legends including Bill Withers, Amy Winehouse, Eric Clapton, and David Gilmour.

British trumpeter Steve Fishwick won the 2002 British Music Awards Rising Star prize and has recorded seven albums on the Hard Bop Records label; his co-led quartet with Southampton-born pianist Leon Greening is dedicated to exploring the music of hard-bop composer Bobby Timmons.

artist_name: Steph Goodwin and The John Crawford Trio
description: Steph Goodwin's recording work includes collaborations with Grammy-nominated producer Mike Stevens, including a 2023 duet with Marc Almond. Pianist John Crawford brings flamenco and Latin fire to his playing, and is recognised as one of the country's leading exponents of Spanish music.

London's Hackney-born New Orleans-style horn ensemble blends pop, drum & bass, funk, and hip-hop through trumpets, trombones, sax, and sousaphone. Named "Most Unique Wedding & Event Brass Band" by the Greater London Enterprise Awards, they are also finalists of the UK London Remixed Brass Off.

A lead vocalist with Cool Million Family and the Urban Voices Collective, London-based singer Janine Johnson has drawn praise from Bond composer David Arnold. Her "Soul in the City" show brings together the classic sounds of Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston and Chaka Khan to PizzaExpress Live Holborn on 12 November.

artist_name: Coltrane 100: Joe Lovano, Melissa Aldana, Nduduzo Makhathini, Linda May Han Oh, Jeff "Tain" Watts
description: Produced with the approval of the Coltrane estate for the centenary of his birth, with Grammy-winning saxophonist Joe Lovano, Chilean tenor Melissa Aldana and South African pianist Nduduzo Makhathini, who draws on McCoy Tyner's legacy. Drummer Jeff “Tain” Watts toured extensively with Alice and Ravi Coltrane.
Trip-hop trio formed in London in 1994 around singer Skye Edwards and brothers Paul and Ross Godfrey. Their debut Who Can You Trust? appeared in 1996, followed by Big Calm in 1998.
Royal Conservatoire of Scotland-trained

artist_name: Emma-Jean Thackray: Dear Miles - A Love Letter
description: Mercury Prize-nominated Leeds trumpeter who stumbled upon Miles Davis as a teenager on a file-sharing site
An ensemble of soloists — including Dee Dee Bridgewater and Jacqui Dankworth — backed by Guy Barker's 44-piece orchestra associated with a major London festival

artist_name: Jean Toussaint Quintet (Opener: Nnamdi Nnachi-Cole Trio)
description: Virgin Islands-born tenor saxophonist who joined Art Blakey's Messengers in 1982 and played on New York Scene, a 1985 Grammy winner. London-based since 1987, he led Brother Raymond (2018), his eleventh album as bandleader.

From County Donegal, Ireland, this teenage fingerstyle guitarist channelled lockdown into a masterclass in Piedmont and ragtime blues. Now signed to Decca Records, her debut album I Kept These Old Blues was reissued on vinyl in February 2025.

Led by French-Chinese guitarist Julien Durand, this London quintet — featuring vocalist Lucy-Anne Daniels and saxophonist George Garford — draws on prog-rock, ambient electronics and Brazilian spirit. Their debut full-length Tales of a Wanderer is available now on LP and CD.

artist_name: Jean Toussaint Quintet (Opening: Nnamdi Nnachi-Cole Trio)
description: A veteran of Art Blakey's Messengers, the US Virgin Islands-born saxophonist returns to the stage with his current working band JT5, whose latest live album Live at the Vortex dropped in August 2025. Opening the night is pianist Nnamdi Nnachi-Cole, a graduate of the Julian Joseph Academy and one of London's most talked-about rising voices.

Debut album Day To Day — released on Ninja Tune and recorded with the support of the Steve Reid Foundation — announced this London-based drummer and tabla player as a singular force. He has since toured with Kamasi Washington and released KAL on Real World Records, bringing Indian classical percussion into vivid conversation with electronics and global sounds.

artist_name: After John – Cosmic Music of Alice Coltrane
description: The harp, the synthesizer, the devotional depth — Alice Coltrane's music is one of the most singular bodies of work in the genre and receives far less attention than her husband's. This tribute arrives at exactly the right moment of renewed critical interest.

Birmingham-based tribute act led by frontman Lionart, whose vocal resemblance to Bob Marley is the centrepiece of the show. The eight-piece backing band, the Hailers, counts members who have shared stages with Pato Banton, Maxi Priest, and the Skatalites, alongside Selecter drummer Charlie "Aitch" Bembridge.

Winners of the City of Derry International Music Award — previously given to Van Morrison and Jools Holland — this British six-piece brings its high-octane swing and jump jive to the Pheasantry. They headlined the first-ever sold-out swing dance at the Royal Albert Hall and have spent over three decades getting rooms on their feet across four continents.

artist_name: PizzaExpress Live Jazz Orchestra feat. Georgia Cécile
Goldie 'Dare to Dream': with his Live Band, Orchestra and Special Guests
description: The 1995 debut album *Timeless* reached number 7 on the UK Albums Chart
Paris-based electro-swing band whose influences span Django Reinhardt, Lionel Hampton, and Daft Punk.

Celebrating her new album Sound of a Woman, this actor-turned-singer blends heartfelt storytelling with soulful pop and Americana. Her Rita Wilson Now & Forever: Duets featured Smokey Robinson, Willie Nelson and Elvis Costello, and her co-write with Sebastián Yatra was shortlisted for an Academy Award.

artist_name: Tony Kofi and The Organisation celebrates 100 years of Lou Donaldson
description: The final surviving member of the original Art Blakey quintet that introduced hard bop, Lou Donaldson moved across bop, hard bop and funk over a seven-decade career without losing his blues-inflected sound. Two-time BBC music award winner Tony Kofi and The Organisation bring that legacy to life, drawing on the organ-driven grooves that defined Donaldson's long run on Blue Note.

Bethlehem-born and largely self-taught, this Palestinian nay master studied at Berklee College of Music and has collaborated with multi-Grammy Award-winning bassist John Patitucci. His three albums — Tripolarity, Nature Addresses You, and Kham — stretch the 5,000-year-old reed flute from melodic to percussive and harmonic dimensions, live and unaccompanied.

artist_name: Jazz on Screen: Miles Davis: The Late Show - A So Watt Special PG
description: A forty-minute BBC Late Show Special, compiled and aired within days of Miles Davis's death in 1991, screens here with exclusive interviews from Herbie Hancock, Quincy Jones, and Max Roach. Clarke Peters performs readings from Davis's autobiography, and Andy Sheppard contributes a special studio performance.

artist_name: Beyond Category & Jeru The Damaja: Honouring Duke Ellington
description: Brooklyn MC Jeru the Damaja, known for his affiliation with Gang Starr and debut album The Sun Rises in the East, joins the ensemble Beyond Category for a rare collision of hip-hop and big band, honouring Duke Ellington, whose fifty-year career produced standards including Mood Indigo and Take the "A" Train.

artist_name: L’Antidote + Naïssam Jalal & Roberto Negro: Landscapes of Eternity
description: Lebanese pianist Rami Khalifé, Albanian cellist Redi Hasa, and Iranian percussionist Bijan Chemirani blend Persian rhythms, Mediterranean traditions and contemporary classical music in L'Antidote, before Naïssam Jalal and Roberto Negro take the stage with Landscapes of Eternity, a project inspired by Jalal's travels through North India, exploring the connections between music, nature and spirituality in the Hindustani tradition.

Mumbai-born vocalist Asha Puthli lent her voice to Ornette Coleman's landmark 1972 album Science Fiction before forging her own path across continents and genres. In 2025, she was inducted into the Women Songwriters Hall of Fame — a fitting honour for an artist whose "Space Talk" has been sampled from hip-hop to house ever since.

Rwandan-born and Belgian-raised, Ineza Kerschkamp fuses the improvisational spirit of neo-soul with her own original compositions. Her 2025 debut album IBUKA arrives backed by a performance history that includes the BBC Concert Orchestra and international touring.

Born in Northern Cyprus, guitarist Okan Ersan released Nibiru, an outer space-inspired concept album named after a mythical planet. Inspired by the 1977 'Wow' signal — believed to be the first alien radio transmission — his Electric Band channels that cosmic reach into live fusion performance.

artist_name: Ari Hoenig Trio featuring Tom Ollendorff and Viktor Nyberg (2 shows)
description: Philadelphia-born drummer Ari Hoenig won the BMW Welt award in Munich — an international competition for best band led by a drummer — and brings his polyrhythmic intensity to the Vortex alongside British guitarist Tom Ollendorff and Swedish bassist Viktor Nyberg, who has toured with artists including Jeremy Pelt, Jackie Terrasson, and Yaron Herman.

artist_name: Buena Vista Social Club Live Revue
description: Inspired by the 1997 Grammy-winning Buena Vista Social Club album, co-produced by Ry Cooder and Juan de Marcos González, this revue brings the sounds of pre-revolutionary Havana to Holborn. Expect an evening of son, bolero, danzón, and cha-cha-cha, performed by some of the UK's finest Cuban musicians.

Indonesian-born, London-based singer-songwriter, LEDI was selected for Spotify's Fresh Finds 2026, its global programme spotlighting emerging independent artists. She brings her blend of bossa nova, soul and pop to PizzaExpress Live to celebrate Golden, her second EP.

The saxophonist who arguably brought British saxophone music to mainstream attention in the late 1980s with his debut Journey to the Urge Within. Four decades on, Pine remains a restless, vital force — his live performances always unpredictable.

artist_name: Lizz Wright with Kenny Banks Sr.
description: A major international music festival. The New York Times called her voice 'a smoky contralto'. Lizz Wright returns after a 20-year career defined by luminous storytelling and soulful grace.
Austrian handpan player who has toured with Björk
Mozambique-born and Lisbon-raised
Two Havana-born Cuban artists with deep Mack Avenue credentials and Grammy nominations between them.

artist_name: Anouar Brahem - After the Last Sky
description: Oud player's first project in eight years, since Blue Maqams, with cellist Anja Lechner and pianist Django Bates; Mats Eilertsen stands in for Dave Holland on bass. The title comes from a line by poet Mahmoud Darwish.
Japanese composer and tenor saxophonist best known for rearranging Bach's complete Cello Suites for solo saxophone.

artist_name: Dave Okumu & Friends present DVTN: Music that Changes the World: from Nina Simone to Sly Stone
description: Vienna-born, Kenyan-heritage guitarist and producer
Oakland-born trumpeter who won the Thelonious Monk International Jazz Competition in 2007

Nine-piece southern soul outfit signed to Hopestreet Recordings, The Meltdown arrive at Café Camden on 15 November for the EFG London Festival. Fronted by vocalist Simon Burke, their 2022 album It's a Long Road and a decade of groove-heavy live shows have earned them a devoted following across Australia and Europe.

Kiya Tabassian, exiled from Iran at 14, founded Montreal's Constantinople in 2001 around a dialogue between Persian tradition and contemporary composition; their partnership with Senegalese kora master Ablaye Cissoko has now yielded a third album. Estuaire, released on Ma Case, is a cycle of intimate musical portraits honouring quiet, real-life figures encountered over years of shared touring.

artist_name: Jazz on Screen: John Coltrane, Soundtracking Cinema: Mo' Better Blues 15
description: Spike Lee's 1990 film was originally titled Love Supreme — inspired by John Coltrane's album A Love Supreme, until his widow Alice Coltrane withdrew permission — making this screening a fitting centenary tribute. The soundtrack is a collaborative album by the Branford Marsalis Quartet and Terence Blanchard, released on Columbia Records.

artist_name: Duo Safar: Imed Alibi & Zied Zouari feat Justin Adams
description: Two of Tunisia's most distinctive musicians — violinist-composer Zied Zouari and percussionist Imed Alibi — revisit the spirit of their acclaimed 2014 album Safar, produced by guest guitarist Justin Adams, whose credits include Robert Plant's Sensational Space Shifters and production work with Tinariwen.

A Boston-born tenor saxophonist who came up playing alongside Charles Mingus and Lionel Hampton, Ford has led bands since his 1977 debut Loxodonta Africana on New World Records. He brings the quartet to World Heart Beat on 15 November.

A Polish-born singer-songwriter who studied in Paris, she released her third album Gdyby kazdy z nas on American label Dot Time Records in 2017. Her second album featured acclaimed singer Basia Trzetrzelewska — expect the same instinct for bold, cross-cultural collaboration at the Pheasantry.

Drawn from players aged 15–25 and mentored by Levitation Orchestra founder Axel Kaner-Lidstrom, this 17-piece big band is the flagship ensemble of a UK organisation now in its 35th year. Their sets mix big band arrangements of standards with hip new arrangements of contemporary tunes and original works.

The London Jazz Orchestra — one of the UK's leading large ensembles — performs a festival special at the Vortex for the EFG London Jazz Festival. Expect ambitious programming and the orchestral scale that makes LJO events genuinely different from anything else on the London scene.

artist_name: MOPOMOSO: International Free Improvised Music – November 2026
description: Established in 1991, Mopomoso is the UK's longest-running concert series dedicated to freely improvised music. Held on the third Sunday of every month at the Vortex, each afternoon brings together a rotating cast of improvisers for unpredictable, in-the-moment musical encounters.

Playing the closing set at a major international music festival in London in 2024, this London six-piece — bass, drums, guitar, keys, sax, and vocals — brings together neo-soul warmth and '90s R&B groove. Their 2025 EP Kismet, recorded live at Dalston Lane Studios, showcases that sound in full.
Grammy-winning New Jersey-born contralto whose My One and Only Thrill took Best Contemporary Album in its category.
Manchester piano trio

artist_name: Float Like a Butterfly: Muhammad Ali
description: A musical portrait of one of the 20th century's most influential figures, this concert draws on music rooted in the Civil Rights Movement, featuring works associated with Louis Armstrong, Miles Davis, Sam Cooke, and James Brown. The programme is curated by Ava Joseph and Ayo Vincent, both World Heart Beat alumni and mentors.

Born out of a Brixton jam night, this London collective counts Joe Armon-Jones, Theon Cross, and Nubiyan Twist among their collaborators. Their debut release Grapefruit balances bold songwriting with seamless technical skill, cementing them as a genuine force on the contemporary scene.

artist_name: Maarja Nuut + Shards 'Combing Hair Into Sand'
description: Shards open before joining Estonian singer and violinist Maarja Nuut for her large-scale song cycle Liivast juukseid kammides at Milton Court, performed with Swiss drummer Nicolas Stocker and rooted in poetry by Estonian writers including Eha Lättemäe. The work sees voice, field recordings and electronics dissolve between fragile intimacy and unsettling intensity.
Scottish Highlands-born
Los Angeles duo whose debut, *Music for Saxofone & Bass Guitar*, was recorded live to tape outside a restaurant and released on Leaving Records.

Budapest-born guitarist Bálint Gyémánt was the first Hungarian student ever to receive a scholarship to the Norwegian Academy of Music in Oslo. His 2024 album The Vortex of Silence — released on 180g vinyl — finds the trio weaving Hungarian roots into a distinctly European sound.

The first Hungarian musician to receive a scholarship to the Norwegian Academy of Music, Budapest guitarist Bálint Gyémánt brings his trio to World Heart Beat. Their 2017 album True Listener on BMC Records featured world-renowned pianist Shai Maestro as a guest, and the group's latest release is The Vortex of Silence.

artist_name: Emilia Martensson/Matt Robinson featuring Adam Waldmann, Max Luthert & Will Glaser

description: A London-based trombonist and composer, trained at the Guildhall School of Music & Drama, brings his distinctive voice to PizzaExpress Live Soho. He is a member of the Mercury Prize-nominated SEED, featured on their critically acclaimed 2019 album Driftglass.

artist_name: Koller/Kofi/Gourlay/Ojumu play Monk feat. Louis Koller
description: Performing at a major London music festival, Tony Kofi joins forces to celebrate Thelonious Monk — one of the most original composers in music history, performed by some of the UK scene's finest players.
scraper_notes: East Side Jazz Club via WeGotTickets

description: Brazilian vocalist touring with string quartet — bossa nova, MPB and improvisation.

artist_name: Andy Sheppard Trio + Norma Winstone & Kit Downes
description: EFG London Jazz Festival double bill — Andy Sheppard Trio with Rita Marcotulli, followed by the extraordinary Norma Winstone with Kit Downes.
Tokyo-based quartet blending harmony, funk and city-pop — their album Prep drew comparisons to Thundercat and Hiatus Kaiyote.

artist_name: A Soul Journey: From Bucharest to London
description: Romanian vocalist Luiza Zan — a composer whose work weaves together folk, classical, and contemporary influences — brings her acclaimed artistry to London for one night. She is joined by Muse Quartet, one of Romania's best-known string ensembles, featuring Alina Horez, Nicoleta Petre, Maria Coltațu, and Alexandra Pascaru.

A Brighton-raised flautist and saxophonist who trained under Binker Golding through Tomorrow's Warriors, Poppy Helmer leads a six-piece band through original compositions drawn from her wonderfully eccentric family upbringing.

artist_name: Reiss Ellis Beckles presents Blues and The Abstract Truth
description: A recreation of Oliver Nelson's 1961 masterpiece — one of the most perfect albums ever recorded, featuring Eric Dolphy, Freddie Hubbard and Bill Evans. Bringing this landmark back to life in a live setting takes courage and musicianship.

A former member — and one-time musical director — of Earth, Wind & Fire, Mo Pleasure is a multi-instrumentalist across piano, bass, trumpet, guitar, drums, and violin. His debut solo album Elements of Pleasure features Philip Bailey, Michael McDonald, and Peabo Bryson.

Nominated for the 2006 Mercury Prize for Melting Pot and winner of the 2012 MOBO Award for Best Act in the genre, this pianist studied at Berklee with Joanne Brackeen and toured with Jerry Dammers' Spatial AKA Orchestra.
Sudanese-British vocalist — East African rhythms and contemporary soul.

Winner of best guitarist at a major 2019 UK music prize, Cartwright brings Picnic — the band she formed with trombonist Annie Whitehead — to Lauderdale House on 19 November. A guitarist and composer who made her name presenting BBC TV's Rockschool, she also toured 17 countries with Afro-Latin group The Guest Stars.

Her 2024 solo debut HERstory on re:freshed cemented her reputation as a sharp-eyed songwriter, with the record funded by the PRS Foundation's Women Make Music and the MOBO Help Musicians Fund. Catch her at PizzaExpress Live Soho on 19 November.

Belfast's Córas Trio bring their second album, Birth Is Upon Me, Death Is Upon Me, to the Vortex on 19 November. Deconstructed Irish traditional melodies emerge from fiddle, guitar and percussion laced with electronics, blending collective free improvisation with seisiún-style playfulness.

artist_name: The London Latin Collective ft. Hetty Loxston
description: A band comprising musicians from Spain, Brazil and the UK, the London Latin Collective brings salsa, cumbia and bossa nova grooves to Holborn. They're joined by classically trained vocalist Hetty Loxston — schooled at Trinity Laban and Bologna's Conservatorio — who spent five years in Italy developing a fluency in Latin, Italian and Brazilian repertoire.

A BRIT School alumna with more than 50 million streams, Oxfordshire-born Tilly Valentine released fan favourite "Table for Two" with South London producer edbl before earning BBC Radio 1 tip of the week. Her soundscape drifts between mellow, soulful works and playful pop, making this Chelsea stop a welcome one.

North London-raised, Ghanaian-heritage multi-instrumentalist Cassius Cobbson released his debut album SANKOFA in 2023, a record that weaves together afrobeat, amapiano, electronica and soul. His debut single 'AKWAABA' earned a feature on the BBC Introducing series via BBC London Radio.

artist_name: When The Roads Meet: Julian Joseph and Alok Verma
description: OBE pianist, composer and BBC Radio 3 broadcaster Julian Joseph meets Alok Verma, who won the Classical Tabla Solo competition at national level in India in 1998, for an evening where British post-bop piano and Indian classical percussion find common ground at their home venue.

artist_name: Trinity Laban String Ensemble and Leon Bosch: Marking 50 years since the Soweto Uprising
description: South African-born double bassist Leon Bosch — a former member of the Academy of St Martin in the Fields — returns to his conservatoire to lead this programme marking half a century since the Soweto Uprising. Bosch has formed the Ubuntu Ensemble with other UK-based South African musicians, bringing a deeply personal connection to the evening's theme.

artist_name: Some Monk and Some Moon: Tina Carr Quintet
description: Her debut, Songs for Curly (self-produced, 2023), earned widespread acclaim; Moon Over Mildmay followed in 2026. For this quintet set, Carr is joined by pianist Matt Robinson and saxophonist Sam Newbould, among other respected collaborators, for an evening of Monk standards and more.

Winners of the 2023 Parliamentary Award for Best Ensemble, this South African-rooted collective features vocalists from KwaZulu-Natal alongside a driving rhythm section and horn players. Their latest album, Tell Me The Truth Or Don't Tell Me Anything, is the backdrop for a live show steeped in Afro-pop, Zulu tradition and infectious groove.

artist_name: The Downstairs Living Presents: Songs of Joni Mitchell with Rebecka Edlund and Immy Churchill
description: Swedish vocalist Rebecka Edlund — whose 2022 debut album Något om en björk was released on her own label Rebecka Aurora — joins City Music Foundation artist and Royal Academy of Music graduate Immy Churchill for an evening devoted to the songs of Joni Mitchell, one of Edlund's three named major influences.

artist_name: Heinen / Vogel / Hitchcock / Bareket / Calderazzo: The Ligeti Project
description: Marking 20 years since the death of György Ligeti, pianist Bruno Heinen — a German-born, London-based professor of composition at Trinity Laban conservatoire — leads this quintet through the avant-garde composer's work. Heidi Vogel, vocalist with the Cinematic Orchestra for over 15 years, joins drummer <cite index="4-4">Gene Calderazzo, whose credits include Pharoah Sanders and Freddie Hubbard.</cite>

artist_name: Heinen / Vogel / Hitchcock / Bareket / Calderazzo / Akki : The Ligeti Project
description: Marking the 20th anniversary of György Ligeti's passing, German-born pianist Bruno Heinen leads this six-piece ensemble through the Hungarian avant-garde composer's work. Vocalist Heidi Vogel, a fixture of the Cinematic Orchestra for over 15 years, joins drummer Gene Calderazzo, whose credits include Pharoah Sanders and Freddie Hubbard.
Performing at a major London music festival, Norwegian trumpeter meets Greek pianist in pure improvised dialogue — two artists from opposite musical climates finding organic common ground.

London-based outfit, winners of the PRS Best New Bands award, their album The Luxury of Time blends Brazilian samba-soul with Latin funk and ska. Drawing influence from the likes of The Dap Kings and Banda Black Rio, expect a high-energy set built for the dance floor.

Greek-born vocalist Eleonora Kouneni marks the release of her new EP Independently Blue on G2 Records — the second instalment of a project reimagining the Great American Songbook. She first made her name in Athens, opening for legendary Greek vocalist Maria Farantouri at the 16th Greek Anti-Racism Festival.

Liverpool-based singer-songwriter who scooped a major FM breakthrough award, Ni Maxine arrives at Soho's best-loved basement with her debut album Mother's Arms, drawing her neo-soul vocals through a lineage running from Billie Holiday to Erykah Badu.

artist_name: Double Bill: Christine Tobin Pseudologia Fantastica + Brian Eley & Ashley Wales's SONGS
description: Dublin-born vocalist Christine Tobin launches her 13th album Pseudologia Fantastica — a meditation on contested realities and misinformation — while Brian Eley, a veteran of the 1977 Ogun vocal quartet Voice alongside Julie Tippett and Phil Minton, pairs with sound artist Ashley Wales of Spring Heel Jack for Songs, a spoken-word and electronic collaboration.

Hackney-born pianist and BBC Young Musician 2020 winner, Gordon has collaborated with Courtney Pine and Ezra Collective, drawing on swing, groove, and his Jamaican heritage. Raised on gospel and reggae, it was a video of Oscar Peterson that switched his path from classical to piano.

Tenor saxophonist and clarinettist who won Best Instrumentalist at the 2007 BBC awards. Swamp (2014, Whirlwind Recordings), by his band Partisans, took Album of the Year at the 2015 Parliamentary awards.

A vocal-led five-piece from the UK, their releases feature collaborations with Robin Mullarkey (Jacob Collier, Natalie Williams) and they are releasing a new EP with producer Chris Hyson (Jordan Rakei, Frida Touray). Kate Lister's powerful vocals anchor high-energy performances that have filled prestigious venues including Band on the Wall and Peggy's Skylight.

Born in Jamaica but raised in Britain, Ciyo Brown is a Hidden Creative Economy Award winner in the 'Best Musician' category (2011) and Lifetime Achievement Award winner (2012). The New York-based singer-songwriter brings her intimate acoustic tour More Than Music: Unplugged to London, featuring the stories and moments behind her songs. Her debut album Lone Rider hit #1 on digital country charts in both the U.S. and U.K., making this an unmissable evening for fans on both sides of the Atlantic.

Named 'Young Artist of the Year' by Jools Holland, this New Forest-born singer-songwriter brings her soul-rooted sound to Holborn. Early sessions with collaborators including Bruno Major and Jimmy Napes (Sam Smith) have helped shape a debut album that blurs genre lines with confidence.
Bassist-led London quintet whose composition 'There is a Crack in Everything' won a coveted Ivor Novello Composer Award.

Formed in 2001, this prize-winning London quartet weaves klezmer with folk traditions from the Balkans, Turkey and Eastern Europe. Their fourth album, First Dance on Second Avenue, was released on Riverboat Records — catch them outdoors at Lauderdale House this August.

artist_name: Tammy Weis with special guest Sarah Moule
description: Edmonton, Alberta-born vocalist Tammy Weis brings her 2023 album Soul Whisper — produced by Portuguese music legend Rui Veloso and set to the poetry of Fernando Pessoa — to the 606 for a special anniversary night. Joining her is Sarah Moule, known for her long association with the late lyricist Fran Landesman and composer Simon Wallace.

The Leicester-born singer-songwriter's 2025 debut album Blue Sky Now arrives at the 606 — a room she's already played — for a December anniversary celebration. Many of its songs were co-written with Michael Garvin, a songwriter behind twenty-three number-one hits for artists including George Benson and Tammy Wynette.

American guitarist Jay Azzolina, a Grammy-nominated veteran of Spyro Gyra, teams up with Galway-born tenor saxophonist Riley Stone-Lonergan for a special anniversary night at the 606 Club. Now UK-based, Azzolina has been active on the British scene since relocating in 2024, and this meeting of transatlantic voices promises to be a night to remember.

artist_name: London Jazz Orchestra Vortex Sessions: The Pianists of the LJO
description: London's longest big band residency turns the spotlight on the keyboard: John Taylor, Pete Saberton, Nikki Iles, and Alcyona Mick — the four pianists who have held the keyboard chair in the LJO — are all original voices as players and writers. Their compositions, and arrangements made by fellow band members, take centre stage at this Vortex Session.

artist_name: Kenny Warren / John Edwards / Andrew Lisle
description: Denver-born trumpeter Kenny Warren, who has released over a dozen albums on labels including Whirlwind Recordings, touches down in London alongside London double bassist John Edwards, one of the most in-demand players in European improvised music, and drummer Andrew Lisle — the pair previously recorded together on Multi-Directional, released on Colin Webster's Raw Tonk label.

artist_name: London Ambient Orchestra Presents: An Evening of Improvised Music and Sonic Exploration
description: Backed by ambient music legends William Basinski and Lubomyr Melnyk, this collaboration of alternative classical artists united through exploration, expression, and experimentation brings their signature collective improvisation to the Vortex. Conservatory-trained classical performers sit alongside self-taught experimental artists, making every performance a genuinely unrepeatable event.

artist_name: Vortex Lates: Jochen Rueckert Quartet plays Jazz Classics
description: Cologne-born drummer Jochen Rueckert has called New York City home since 1997, appearing on over 120 albums alongside names including Pat Metheny, Ron Carter, and Kurt Rosenwinkel. His quartet brings a programme of classics to Dalston for one late-night set.

Cologne-born drummer Jochen Rueckert has called New York City home since 1997, and his new quartet features trumpeter Alexandra Ridout, tenor saxophonist Kevin Sun, and bassist Hamish Smith. All three are around two decades his junior — a deliberate choice for a bandleader whose previous quartet with Mark Turner and Lage Lund toured worldwide for over 15 years.

Debut album The Chase was picked by The Times as one of its Top 10 Albums of 2017 across all genres, and the follow-up, Move (Ubuntu Music), landed five stars in BBC Music Magazine. Tenor saxophonist Richardson brings his hard-driving quartet to the Vortex on 7 November.

Brought together by saxophonist Caroline Kraabel, this large collective of women and trans/non-binary improvisers returns to the Vortex, where they recorded their live album Live at The Vortex July 2024, released in December 2024.

This quartet — Alex Bonney (trumpet), Olie Brice (bass), George Crowley (sax) and Tim Giles (drums) — formed during lockdown to explore the music of Ornette Coleman, later expanding into Don Cherry, Dewey Redman and Arthur Blythe. Bonney also works as a studio engineer and producer for artists on leading labels including ECM.

London pianist Finn Carter blends soul, hip-hop and free music into his own uncompromising compositional voice, with his latest album Finding Home out on Whirlwind Recordings. He experiments with form alongside dancer Stephanie Burrell, in a rare meeting of improvised piano and movement.

Bringing together trumpeter Chris Batchelor of Loose Tubes and electric bassist Tom Herbert of Polar Bear, alongside Allsopp's saxophone and bass clarinet, this ensemble performs original compositions at the Vortex on 21 November. A BBC Award for Innovation winner in 2008, Allsopp leads the group through the evening.

artist_name: Steve Noble, Caius Williams & Tom Challenger
description: A former member of Rip Rig and Panic, drummer Steve Noble brings his ultra-detailed percussion to this trio with London bassist Caius Williams and saxophonist Tom Challenger, who leads Brass Mask — a group rooted in traditional street-music and collective improvisation. Williams and Challenger have an ongoing collaboration releasing recordings made at the GRAIN residency in Bermondsey.

artist_name: Out Front + Olie Brice Quartet (Double Bill)
description: Out Front, a UK quintet rooted in the music of Booker Little and Andrew Hill, now performs entirely original work composed across the band's membership. Olie Brice leads his Quartet — featuring Rachel Musson, Alexander Hawkins, and Will Glaser — whose debut album All It Was was released in 2025.

London trumpeter and composer Mark Kavuma leads The Banger Factory, a 20-plus-piece collective that has grown into its own label. Their 2024 album Magnum Opus, released on Banger Factory Records, brings that same sprawling, hard-bop-rooted energy to the Vortex stage.

artist_name: The Commission for New and Old Art presents: I Am Nobody – London Show

description: Swiss-born pianist, singer and composer, her album Thrive won "Recording of the Year" at the Presto Music Awards 2025. Trained at the Lucerne School of Music, she also studied with guitarist Gwilym Simcock, bringing a blend of folk-inflected melody and improvisation to the Vortex stage.

artist_name: John Butcher / Phil Durrant / Mark Wastell
description: English saxophonist John Butcher, London College of Music-trained violinist and improviser Phil Durrant, and cellist and Confront Recordings founder Mark Wastell — three veterans of the British free improvisation scene — reunite at the Vortex. Butcher and Durrant share a long history, having previously recorded Secret Measures together and collaborated in the celebrated trio with John Russell.

British-Iranian guitarist Karim Saber brings his quintet to the Vortex, fresh from touring Europe with Lukas DeRungs' Kosmos Suite, nominated for a 2023 German Music Prize. His debut album Transmission (Ubuntu Music) was followed by a second record, Sundance, released in 2026.

artist_name: Basil Hodge Quartet Featuring Tony Kofi
description: Pianist and composer Basil Hodge brings his hard-swinging quartet to the Vortex, drawing on material from his critically acclaimed album A Point of Reference. Joining him is multi-award-winning saxophonist Tony Kofi, a two-time BBC and two-time Parliamentary Award winner whose status as the first UK-born musician in David Murray's World Saxophone Quartet speaks for itself.

Named Best Musician of the Year at the 2009 Parliamentary Awards, British guitarist Phil Robson brings his organ trio to the Vortex — the format that showcases his most imaginative composing. A career split between London and New York has seen him work alongside Billy Hart, Kenny Wheeler, and Dave Liebman.

artist_name: London Jazz Orchestra with the Essex Youth Jazz Orchestra

description: A UK saxophonist and composer whose debut album Light Manoeuvres (New Dawn) featured LA percussion polymath Carlos Niño, Spilsbury brings new music and improvisations to the Vortex with a quintet. His collaborators also span Iglooghost, Nate Mercereau and Surya Botofasina, alongside a long-standing role in avant-rock experimentalists The Physics House Band.

artist_name: Frank Carlberg with the Trinity Laban Jazz Orchestra (Two Shows)
description: Helsinki-born pianist and composer Frank Carlberg — who has recorded and performed with Bob Brookmeyer, Roswell Rudd, and Kenny Wheeler — joins the Trinity Laban Orchestra, led by saxophonist and improviser Mark Lockheart, for two shows at the Vortex. Carlberg's Large Ensemble recordings Monk Dreams, Hallucinations and Nightmares and Elegy for Thelonious earned four-and-a-half and five stars respectively from DownBeat.

A founding member of the celebrated Loose Tubes big band, saxophonist Mark Lockheart brings his new chordless trio to the Vortex on 12 December. Their debut album Shapeshifter, out on Subtone Records, strips things to saxophone, bass and drums — letting the music flow freely without a harmony instrument in sight.

artist_name: Being Human – Minar of Dreams (Album Launch)
description: A pan-European quartet — Lithuanian guitarist Mindaugas Stumbras, Scottish pianist Fergus McCreadie, Italian bassist Michelangelo Scandroglio, and Italian drummer Mattia Galeotti — their repertoire combines original compositions with pieces drawn from folk traditions, and they bring their new album Minar of Dreams, released under exclusive license to Bridge The Gap, to the Vortex for its London launch.

artist_name: Finn Carter, Matt Carmichael & Alex Hitchcock
description: Pianist Finn Carter's latest album Finding Home on Whirlwind Recordings brings him to the Vortex alongside Scottish saxophonist Matt Carmichael, whose album Marram on Edition Records won Best Album at the Scottish Awards, and Ivor Novello-nominated composer and saxophonist Alex Hitchcock.

Winner of the ISJAC prize for Emerging Black Composers, this British multi-instrumentalist of Nigerian and Jamaican descent brings her trio to Dalston for one night. Her credits include appearing on Decca Records' Alone Together piano album and graduating Magna Cum Laude from Berklee College of Music.

artist_name: Ian Shaw’s New Year’s Eve Bash
description: Widely regarded as the finest male vocal talent the UK has produced, Welsh vocalist Ian Shaw has recorded 16 studio albums spanning three decades. His most recent release, Stephensong – Ian Shaw Sings Stephen Sondheim (2025), sees him partnered by pianist Barry Green at the Vortex.

Led by award-winning reed player and pianist Ewan Bleach, the Procrastinators weave Balkan and Gypsy folk, swing, tangos and standards into one gloriously unpredictable set. Expect good company, normal prices, and midnight arriving whenever their famous "special clock" decides.

Talkline — the duo of vocalist and vibraphone player Amy Hollingsworth and pianist Will Hobson — recorded their self-titled debut EP at Abbey Road Studios, released in July 2024. Their sound blurs the lines between singer-songwriter, minimalism and improvisation, drawing on influences from Lucy Rose and Hiatus Kaiyote to Steve Reich.

Her debut album Take My Hand, released in 2025, blends folk, indie pop, and singer-songwriter craft with a distinct feel for groove and space. An Australian-born cellist and vocalist, she has shared stages with Nitin Sawhney at the Royal Albert Hall and performed at the BBC Proms.

The British pianist behind Twentysomething — the fastest-selling British debut in history — returns to one of London's most storied rooms. A two-time BRIT Award winner who also picked up a Golden Globe nomination for co-writing the Gran Torino theme with Clint Eastwood, Cullum brings his signature genre-blurring piano showmanship to Soho on 11 November.

Detroit's youngest-ever resident artist at Cliff Bell's, saxophonist Houston Patton brings his hard-swinging range — from gospel to hard bop — to Leicester Square. His 2024 debut album Here We Are, recorded with his quintet Quintessential, showcases the Detroit collective he leads.

Lead vocalist for Incognito since 2023, the Nottingham-raised singer-pianist brings her latest album, Black Moon, released in March 2026, to Soho for one night. Signed to Decca Records after her debut album Devil in Me, she has since built a loyal following on her own terms — expect piano, soul, and serious vocal range.

Vocalist, trumpeter, and arranger who was nominated for Artist of the Year at the 2024 Boisdale Music Awards, Muoneké is also a nominee for Vocalist of the Year at a major music awards ceremony in 2026. His debut album, The Young Man With The Old Soul, was released in October 2020.

A London-based vocalist and songwriter, she has performed her single "Greenlight" with a full orchestra at The Barbican, and collaborated with American duo Smoakland Beats at the Red Rocks Amphitheatre in 2023. Expect an evening of original songs woven together with classic standards, drawn from her favourite female vocalists.

Her writing credits include contributions to the Creed III soundtrack for J. Cole's Dreamville label, and vocals on a track produced by Wu-Tang Clan's RZA. The Swiss-Polish, London-based singer-songwriter brings her blend of soul, R&B, and pop to the Pheasantry on the back of her sold-out Purple To Blue release show.

From Crewe, this blues-soul pianist has shared stages with Gregory Porter and Jamie Cullum, and famously played alongside Jools Holland at his Boogie Woogie & Blues Spectacular. His Sky TV series Tom Seals Presents sees him perform live arrangements of celebrities' favourite songs.

Members have performed on ITV's Britain's Got Talent, at the O2 Arena, and live on FM radio, bringing their original arrangements of soul, funk, disco, and R&B to PizzaExpress Live Holborn for a festive evening of seasonal classics and groove.

Raleigh's Jamil Rashad brought in Blake Rhein of Durand Jones & the Indications and Colin Croom of Twin Peaks for Electric Cowboy: Born in Carolina Mud, released on Normaltown Records. His follow-up, Carolina Funk: Barn Burner on Tobacco Road, is described as a more accurate reflection of his electrifying live show.

From Crewe, this blues-soul pianist has shared stages with Gregory Porter and Jamie Cullum, and famously played alongside Jools Holland at his Boogie Woogie & Blues Spectacular. His Sky TV series Tom Seals Presents sees him perform live arrangements of celebrities' favourite songs.

A BEFFTA Award winner and pianist based in London, he founded the Kudos Gospel Choir, named BBC Songs of Praise Gospel Choir of the Year 2024. He has performed alongside the Kingdom Choir, featured at the 2018 Royal Wedding, and appears as featured pianist on recordings including Tracey Campbell's Simply Hymn.

London-born singer-pianist Jordan Jackson, now Copenhagen-based, has toured with US artist Son Little and performed alongside prolific Danish pianist Niels Lan Doky. Her set draws on her CD Footprints alongside newer singles including "Soul of a Woman" and "Blue is for the Sky."

Their 1989 album The Big Area went gold and peaked at number four on the UK Albums Chart. Singer Mark Shaw now performs regularly as Then Jerico Acoustic, bringing those hits to an intimate PizzaExpress Live setting this December.

Led by musical director Paul Burch, the band takes its name from the London street long regarded as the heart of the British music scene. Performing compositions that span an entire century of music, they bring the swinging sounds of the big band era to life at PizzaExpress Live Holborn on 20 December.

London's Latin Bridge, created by guitarist Sergio Marciano Pereda in 2016, brings bossa nova, Cuban son and standards to PizzaExpress Live Holborn. They're joined by Divyarup — a Brazilian singer, guitarist and songwriter whose album Tempo de Luz draws on the sounds of Brazil, and who has performed at London's Roundhouse.

Guardian restaurant critic and MasterChef judge Jay Rayner leads his six-piece band through sharp new arrangements of 80s chart hits — Sade, Sting, Swing Out Sister — that always had swing at their core. Since forming in 2012, the group has played Ronnie Scott's and King's Place, making this Soho date a reliable fixture for the band's devoted following.

This UK 10-piece reached No. 1 on the iTunes chart with their single When I Fall in Love and have sold out nine shows at Ronnie Scott's. Their set draws on the swing era repertoire of Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Louis Armstrong, and Ella Fitzgerald.

Debut EP The Birds picked up airplay from both Cerys Matthews on BBC 6 Music and Jamie Cullum on BBC Radio 2. Pianist Lior Solomons-Wise, who crafted the string arrangements, returns alongside Axton for an evening rooted in her Lake District-inspired songwriting.

South East London's ten-piece brass collective have played Glastonbury and supported Basement Jaxx on their way to becoming one of the capital's most riotous live draws. Their 2016 debut album was followed by a brass reimagining of Radiohead's "Paranoid Android," complete with a live-action remake of the original Magnus Carlsson animation.

Widely celebrated as the First Lady of West End musicals, her debut album Anthems featured Queen guitarist Brian May and Foo Fighters' Taylor Hawkins on drums. The record reached number 15 on the UK Albums Chart, announcing a voice that belongs just as powerfully on an intimate stage as a grand one.

A cross-channel collective uniting musicians from London and Paris in shared devotion to the sounds of the 50s and 60s. Washington D.C.-born tenor saxophonist Harry Allen — best known for his work with John Pizzarelli and Bucky Pizzarelli — brings his warm, mainstream swing to the reunion.

Winner of the Des Simmonds young guitarist award and the NYJO guitar chair at 18, this London-born guitarist released his self-titled debut on Fresh Sound New Talent. A sought-after collaborator, he has performed alongside Jamie Cullum, Jason Rebello, and Alexandra Ridout.

A London-based vocalist and composer who blends folk and contemporary sounds, Noble was a finalist in the 2025 Tina May Young Musician competition. Her debut album New Eve — a voice and bass duo recorded with 2024 BBC Young Musician winner Ursula Harrison — came out in April 2026.

Praised by Chick Corea for her "beautiful and creative arrangements and renditions," this New York-born vocalist, pianist, and composer brings her quintet to Soho. Her catalogue spans nine albums, most recently On the Brink, with sold-out shows at this very venue already under her belt.

West End performers from shows including Les Misérables, Phantom of the Opera, and Wicked gather for this musical theatre cabaret series, now in its seventh year at this very venue. Musical Director Ian MacGregor accompanies the cast as they bring favourite songs from musicals old and new over Sunday lunch.

Drummer Matt Skelton's ensemble is dedicated to the music of Shelly Manne, drawing inspiration from his 1959 album Live At The Blackhawk, recorded at the famous San Francisco club. The band connects with the music of the original artists while bringing their own originality to every performance.

Milan-born alto saxophonist Tommaso Starace moved to the UK in 1994, and his trio's live debut, Live at the Beaver Inn, was released on Dodicilune Records. He has performed alongside Billy Cobham, David Liebman, and Kenny Wheeler, and brings that pedigree to a Hammond organ-driven trio at PizzaExpress Live Soho.

His debut album, Hand Built by Robots, entered the UK charts at number three before climbing to the top in 2007. The Surrey-born singer-songwriter returns with material spanning a catalogue that now stretches to his 2025 album Octopus, including recent singles featuring Lissie and Los Bitchos.

A Newcastle soul outfit built around the songwriting and vocal talents of Louise Mehan, whose single "Love Don't Come That Easy" topped the prestigious soul chart. Mehan has shared the stage with Candy Stayton and recorded alongside Detroit soulstress Kathy Kosins.

artist_name: Sara Oschlag with Echoes of Ellington Jazz Orchestra
description: Danish-born vocalist Sara Oschlag joins Peter Long's London-based big band, assembled from musicians chosen for their individual sounds matching the original Ellington sidemen. Together they explore the Duke Ellington and Ella Fitzgerald songbook, with Oschlag — whose 2024 album YEAH! drew widespread critical praise — bringing her singular voice to one of the great big band repertoires.

A Newcastle soul outfit built around the songwriting and vocal talents of Louise Mehan, whose single "Love Don't Come That Easy" topped the prestigious soul chart. Mehan has shared the stage with Candy Stayton and recorded alongside Detroit soulstress Kathy Kosins.

Two-time BBC Award winner Ian Shaw joins Parliamentary Awards Best Vocalist 2021 Georgia Mancio for an intimate evening at PizzaExpress Live Soho. Shaw's most recent album, Stephensong – Ian Shaw Sings Stephen Sondheim, makes him a natural foil for Mancio, whose partnership with double Grammy-winning pianist Alan Broadbent has produced three acclaimed albums.

Two-time BBC Award winner Ian Shaw shares the stage with Claire Martin OBE, honoured for her services to music at the Queen's Birthday Honours in 2011. Shaw's most recent album, Stephensong – Ian Shaw Sings Stephen Sondheim, arrived in 2025, while Martin has released more than 20 albums on Linn Records — two voices, one unmissable night in Soho.

A two-time BBC Award winner for Best Vocalist, Ian Shaw brings his most recent project — Stephensong, a celebration of Stephen Sondheim — to the PizzaExpress stage. Joining him is Natalie Williams, a former lead vocalist with UK Acid collective Incognito, and a MOBO Award nominee for Best UK Soul.

artist_name: Ian Shaw with Iain Ballamy and Jamie Safir
description: Three-time award winner Ian Shaw brings his warm Welsh baritone to Soho alongside ECM recording artist Iain Ballamy and Manchester-born pianist Jamie Safir — the trio behind the 2020 album What's New. Safir holds a co-writing credit on Shaw's Greek Street Friday, making this a reunion of three musicians with deep creative roots.

Welsh-born singer, pianist and songwriter Ian Shaw brings his Pianobar show to PizzaExpress Live Soho on 28 January. His most recent album, Stephensong – Ian Shaw Sings Stephen Sondheim (2025), was made in partnership with pianist Barry Green.

A BRIT School graduate, Wendi Harriott has recorded and performed with artists including John Legend and Jennifer Hudson, and contributed backing vocals to Emeli Sandé's album Our Version of Events. Catch her headline set at PizzaExpress Live Holborn on 28 January.

Three-time award winner Ian Shaw brings his velvet voice to Soho alongside saxophonist Tony Kofi — the first UK-born musician to join David Murray's World Saxophone Quartet. The pair previously recorded An Adventurous Dream: The Music of Billy Strayhorn and Duke Ellington together, making this a reunion worth catching.

Welsh-born singer, pianist and songwriter Ian Shaw brings his Pianobar show to PizzaExpress Live Soho on 28 January. His most recent album, Stephensong – Ian Shaw Sings Stephen Sondheim (2025), was made in partnership with pianist Barry Green.

Two-time winner of the BBC's top vocalist prize in the genre, Ian Shaw brings his 16-album career to Soho alongside Elaine Delmar, who sang at the Barbican with Wynton Marsalis and the Lincoln Center Big Band and whose most recent album, Speak Low, was released on the Ubuntu label. Two of Britain's most decorated vocal talents, one intimate room.

A two-time BBC Award winner for Best Vocalist, Shaw brings his most recent project — Stephensong, a tribute to Stephen Sondheim with pianist Barry Green — to a familiar London stage. With 16 studio albums across three decades, he remains widely regarded as the finest male vocal voice the UK has produced.

British soul pioneers who recruited Bob Dylan for his Desire sessions in 1975, Kokomo bring their four-vocalist groove to Holborn. Their debut album was hailed by the NME as the best debut by a British band in several years.
A lunchtime session with Ian Shaw and Polly Gibbons at PizzaExpress Live Soho, starting at 1.00pm.

A three-time award winner — twice BBC Best Vocalist and once at the Parliamentary Awards — Ian Shaw brings his rich, storytelling voice to Soho. He's joined by MBE trumpeter Guy Barker, whose collaborators have ranged from Frank Sinatra to Ornette Coleman.

UK No.1 winner at the 2018 National Tribute Music Awards, Oye Santana honours five decades of Carlos Santana's catalogue — from Woodstock-era classics to multi-million sellers like Smooth and Black Magic Woman. Frontman Milan draws on deep roots in Latin rock, blues, and fusion to deliver note-for-note recreations of solos straight from the original recordings.

British trumpeter Steve Fishwick won the 2002 British Music Awards Rising Star prize and has recorded seven albums on the Hard Bop Records label; his co-led quartet with Southampton-born pianist Leon Greening is dedicated to exploring the music of hard-bop composer Bobby Timmons.

artist_name: The Wonder of Stevie – The Music of Stevie Wonder
description: Vocalist Noel McCalla — voted one of Britain's top soul singers by Blues and Soul Magazine — leads this six-piece alongside award-winning saxophonist Derek Nash, a member of Jools Holland's Rhythm and Blues Orchestra since 2004. Expect a sweeping set drawing from Signed, Sealed, Delivered, Talking Book, Innervisions, Songs in the Key of Life, and Hotter than July.

In 2025 they were enlisted to back New York trumpet icon Tom Browne at the Saturday Love festival, bringing the same dancefloor heat to PizzaExpress Live Holborn this December.

Founded in 1965 and an Arts Council England National Portfolio Organisation, NYJO's Under 18s programme puts the next generation of musicians centre stage. This learning programme for under 18s brings fresh young talent to Soho for an evening of big band energy this February.

London guitarist and composer Ross Ian Lardner leads this fusion trio, whose 2025 album Interplanetary Funk was made alongside Yellowjackets bassist Jimmy Haslip. Expect Holdsworth-inspired phrasing and a night of wide-ranging sonic exploration.
A Royal College of Music graduate, she co-leads The Maddie Martin Big Band alongside trumpeter and composer Gabriel Taylor. Her debut album Part One is scheduled for release in early 2027.

Award-winning Norwegian drummer and composer Snorre Kirk leads this pan-European quartet, whose lineup brings together saxophonist Giacomo Smith and pianist Joe Webb from the British scene, alongside Danish bassist Anders Fjeldsted. Their 2021 Stunt Records album Going Up was recorded in Copenhagen — expect that same driving swing delivered live in Soho.

A session musician for Michael Bublé who went on to tour with Seal and Michael Bolton, this American saxophonist brings her Latin-inflected sound to Soho. Her debut album Tequila Moon on Peak Records produced a Billboard #1 single of the same name.

Three funky female singers front a rocking five-piece band, this London outfit puts an original twist on funk, R&B and blues. Fresh from recording and promoting their EP on Breaking Records, they've played the Cork Guinness Festival and the St. Louis Festival in Sète, France.

Led by original Animals drummer John Steel, Animals & Friends bring the Newcastle band's legendary catalogue to Holborn. The Animals were the second British band to top the American charts after The Beatles, with House of the Rising Sun.

artist_name: Ian McNabb of The Icicle Works Acoustic
description: The Mercury-nominated Liverpool songwriter behind The Icicle Works has recorded and performed alongside Crazy Horse and Ringo Starr. His band's hits "Love Is A Wonderful Colour" and "Whisper To A Scream (Birds Fly)" reached the Top 40 on both sides of the Atlantic. Now he revisits that catalogue in an intimate acoustic setting at PizzaExpress Live Holborn.

Bassist Arnie Somogyi and pianist Mark Edwards have recorded The Ellington Piano Project, reimagining Duke Ellington's final public performance. Edwards has also spent a decade touring the world as pianist for Katie Melua, bringing pop-honed precision to an evening of deep swing and Ellingtonian colour.

Featuring Mercury Prize-nominated Scottish pianist Fergus McCreadie alongside Lithuanian guitarist Mindaugas Stumbras and a Tuscan rhythm section, this pan-European quartet folds folk traditions from four distinct homelands into lyrical melodic storytelling. They headline PizzaExpress Live Soho on 15 April 2027.

A Liverpool-born songwriter, drummer and producer, his debut album This Is Nowhere. This Is Everywhere features UK drumming legend Steve White. Signed to German label Agogo Records, he brings his groove-heavy soul-funk sound to Soho on 28 April.

Debut album The Chase was picked by The Times as one of its Top 10 Albums of 2017 across all genres, and the follow-up, Move (Ubuntu Music), landed five stars in BBC Music Magazine. Tenor saxophonist Richardson brings his hard-driving quartet to the Vortex on 7 November.

artist_name: Jazz at Cockpit: Matt Seddon + Calum Gourlay Big Band
description: Derby-born trombonist and composer Matt Seddon has built a reputation on the London scene alongside names like Charles Tolliver and the Ronnie Scott's Orchestra. Joining forces is Glasgow bassist Calum Gourlay, whose 2019 album New Ears earned an Ivor Novello Composer Award nomination and who leads a monthly big band residency at the Vortex.

artist_name: Frank Carlberg with the Trinity Laban Jazz Orchestra
description: A Helsinki-born pianist who has recorded and performed with Bob Brookmeyer, Roswell Rudd, and Steve Lacy, Carlberg brings his Large Ensemble vision to London — his 2024 release Elegy for Thelonious earned five stars from DownBeat — joining forces with the Trinity Laban conservatoire orchestra, led by saxophonist Mark Lockheart, a showcase for the conservatoire's final-year composers and improvisers.

Has been at the forefront of modern UK improvised music, leaning towards the modal approach to improvisation. Citing influences such as trumpeters; Miles Davis, Freddie Hubbard, Hannibal Lokumbe, Lester Bowie, and Don Cherry.

artist_name: The Maydan Ensemble - Of The North London Jazz Collective
description: The Maydan Ensemble of the North London Jazz Collective is a quintet that blends modern jazz with Arabic, Anatolian and Persian folk music.
On SATURDAY 14th November we present Daense
On Thursday 19th November we present - Echoes of Naná.

Smiodair — Irish for fragments or small broken pieces — is an international quartet playing original music that moves constantly between composition and improvisation. Thunderous grooves collide with dreamlike sonic landscapes; without a harmony instrument, the music is raw and direct, rich in melody and rhythm. The name also reflects the musicians’ paths, diverging and reconnecting across London,

Rooted in contemporary fusion, British-Sicilian trombonist and composer Laura Impallomeni puts the trombone front and centre with her original compositions.

artist_name: Yoruba, Konkani, and Columbian Christmas by The Inner Vision Trio
description: Part of the Inner Vision Orchestra of blind musicians established by Baluji Shrivastav OBE, this trio — soprano Victoria Oruwari, violist and vocalist Takashi Kikuchi, and pianist and vocalist Kevin Satizabal — bring Christmas songs from Yoruba, Konkani, and Colombian traditions to Lauderdale House for one festive evening.

A vocalist who has performed at the Elgar Room at the Royal Albert Hall and Ronnie Scott's, Houlder graduated from the University of Birmingham with a First Class Honours degree in Music. Catch her at World Heart Beat on 29 November.

Featured in the BBC's list of "100 Greats," saxophonist Iain Ballamy joins British Award-winning pianist Gareth Williams for an intimate duo set at World Heart Beat. Ballamy's recordings span from his 1988 debut Balloon Man to his 2025 Babel Label release Riversphere, a career-long arc of restless invention that promises a compelling evening.

artist_name: Filomena Campus Quartet: Theatraliawith Steve Lodder, Rod Youngs and Charlie Pyne
description: Sardinian vocalist, lyricist and theatre director Filomena Campus presents Theatralia, with pianist Steve Lodder, who has worked with Andy Sheppard across several long-running projects. The quartet weaves music and improvisation with spoken word, poetry and comic sketches, rooting Campus's Mediterranean identity in a contemporary sound with an electronic twist.

Trained by Orlando López "Cachaito" of Buena Vista Social Club, the Cuban double bassist brings Havana to Soho with his quintet. A veteran of Oscar Valdés' Diakara Orchestra and the Netflix series The Eddy, Nueva has also collaborated on a Latin Grammy-nominated project alongside John Legend and Roberto Fonseca.

One of the UK's finest big bands, led by award-winning bandleader Pete Long, the orchestra draws on classics by Count Basie, Duke Ellington, Stan Kenton and The Rat Pack. Expect roaring swing, sassy vocals, fabulous funk and delicious Latin flavours from a band packed with first-call players.

artist_name: Trio Grande - Gilad Hekselman/Will Vinson/Nate Wood
description: Israeli-born guitarist Gilad Hekselman joins British-American saxophonist Will Vinson and Grammy-nominated drummer and multi-instrumentalist Nate Wood for a rare outing as Trio Grande, the group whose debut album landed in 2020. Hekselman won the 2005 Gibson Montreux International Guitar Competition, and this Ronnie Scott's date puts all three voices on equal footing — no piano, nowhere to hide.

Grammy-nominated Hammond B3 organist Pat Bianchi brings his 2026 album Confluence to life at Ronnie Scott's, with saxophonist Troy Roberts and drummer Colin Stranahan. A longtime member of late guitar icon Pat Martino's trio, Bianchi is one of the instrument's most seasoned and sought-after voices.

Parliamentary Vocalist of the Year (2024), Emma Smith recently toured with American supergroup Postmodern Jukebox and now brings her swinging Great American Songbook artistry to Ronnie's. She's joined by pianist Jamie Safir and his trio, celebrating the release of Momentism, his debut album as bandleader and composer.

Named a DownBeat 2025 Critics Poll Rising Star Artist of the Year, this Mongolian-born pianist and composer brings her quartet to Ronnie Scott's to perform Bright Folk, her third album, released November 2026. Born in Ulaanbaatar in 1998, Erdenebaatar began in classical composition before turning to the piano programme at Munich's Hochschule für Musik und Theater.

American saxophonist Dave Lewis leads this quartet — the tight rhythm section also powering his eight-piece band 1UP — through Blue Note classics, rare groove favourites, and originals, with sidemen who have shared stages with George Benson, Gregory Porter, and Hugh Masekela.

South London composer and multi-instrumentalist Dominic Canning — aka DoomCannon — served as Musical Director for award-winning vocalist Celeste, performing live at the Brit Awards and Later with Jools Holland. His debut single 'Amalgamation' was released via Brownswood Recordings, the label that also backed his 2022 album Renaissance.

Declared a "Bass Ace" by Bass Player magazine, the Greek double bassist has collaborated closely with Arooj Aftab, featuring prominently at her BBC Proms debut as bassist and orchestrator. He brings pianist Kristjan Randalu and drummer Ziv Ravitz to Ronnie Scott's, previewing new material ahead of a forthcoming 2026 album release.

São Paulo's keyboard-bass-drums trio bring their golden-era Brazilian funk-samba to Ronnie Scott's. Their 2024 album Modo Avião, released on Far Out Recordings, follows 2020's Angela — hailed by BBC 6 Music and Gilles Peterson as one of the best albums of that year.

Keyboardist and composer for George Michael, Amy Winehouse, and Chaka Khan, Smith brings his piano and Hammond organ mastery to Ronnie's for an evening of gospel, funk, and soul. His 2021 debut album It's Time featured a collaboration with vibraphone legend Roy Ayers, and that same spirit of spontaneous groove drives The Metamorph Project live.

Grandson of trumpet legend Doc Cheatham, this Grammy-nominated Florida-born trumpeter blends post-bop, funk, and hip-hop into a singular sound. His horn has graced platinum records by J. Cole and Ari Lennox, but Ronnie Scott's is where he brings it all back to the bandstand.

Birmingham-born songwriter and multi-instrumentalist, her debut album Lover's Discourse is out via Portland's Eulipion Arts. She has opened for Louis Cole and Braxton Cook, bringing her psychedelic soul and R&B to Ronnie Scott's on 7 November.

Leeds-based saxophonist and producer whose work spans footwork, hip-hop, and UK electronic music, his latest release Voices Through the Wall is out on XVI Records. The record features rapper Open Mike Eagle, and the band brings that same blend of live woodwind and electronic weight to Upstairs at Ronnie's.

Expect classics from BB King, Buddy Guy, Peter Green, Muddy Waters and Howlin' Wolf, delivered by a band whose pedigree spans Chicago to the Delta.

A twice winner of the British Blues Award for Best Acoustic Performer and Best Songwriter, this London guitarist leads The Ronnie Scott's Blues Explosion at their long-running monthly residency at the very venue he returns to now. He also served as frontman of British blues rock group Ten Years After from 2014 until 2024.

Formed to mark the 40th anniversary of Ozone's international debut, TRiNFiNiTY pairs the Kobe-born pianist with bassist Shimpei Ogawa and drummer Kunito Kitai. Their 2024 debut album TRiNFiNiTY on Universal Music, followed by acclaimed 2026 follow-up For Someone, has rapidly established the trio as one of the most exciting groups on the contemporary scene.

artist_name: Ronnie Scott's Classical All Stars present Gershwin and The American Classics
description: Directed by pianist James Pearson, the seven-piece Classical All Stars ensemble brings together some of the UK's leading session musicians for an evening of re-arrangements of Gershwin, Copland and Bernstein. The programme culminates in a full performance of Rhapsody in Blue, over 100 years since its UK premiere.

Signed to Linn Records, his album New Songs for Old Souls earned five-star reviews and was named one of the Telegraph's best albums of 2015. The son of lyricist and entertainer Sir Richard Stilgoe, he brings a rich theatrical instinct to the bandstand — expect an evening of wit, swing, and piano-led charm at Ronnie Scott's.

Oslo's award-winning piano trio arrives fresh from their fifth album, Entropies, released on Svale Records in 2026. Pianist Espen Berg became an official Steinway Artist in 2023, leading a trio whose tightly-knit interplay has earned devoted audiences across Europe and Japan.

Stockholm-born vocalist Liselotte Östblom, who has collaborated with drummer Gregory Hutchinson, joins pianist Jamie Safir's trio to celebrate his debut bandleader album Momentism, drawing on the melodic lyricism of Bill Evans and the post-bop rhythms of Ahmad Jamal.

Son of Dave Brubeck, pianist Darius leads his London-based quartet to Ronnie Scott's to launch their new album Live Again, following sold-out dates across France, Italy, and the UK. Their previous record, Live in Poland (Ubuntu Music), was named among Downbeat magazine's best releases of 2020.

Born in Jerusalem and raised in Buenos Aires, Bareket took first prize at the International Society of Bassists' competition in 2011 and returns to the stage behind his new Enja Records release, AYIN. His quartet features alto saxophonist Godwin Louis, pianist Esteban Castro, and drummer Savannah Harris.

A Los Angeles-born trumpeter who forged an early bond with the Mingus Big Band, Pelt has since performed alongside Ravi Coltrane, Roy Hargrove, and Cassandra Wilson. A prolific recording artist, he has released a new album on HighNote Records every year since 2010.

Brooklyn-born drummer and producer Lyndon Harewood — aka Gengis Don — makes his Ronnie Scott's debut backed by a tight quartet including tenor saxophonist Devaughn Durham. His credits span Solange, A$AP Ferg, Bilal and Roy Hargrove, with hip-hop and improvisation woven into a single, groove-locked whole.

A sixteen-year member of John McLaughlin's 4th Dimension, this Leeds-born drummer and keyboardist now leads his newly formed Orbital Band. His Dirty & Beautiful albums on Abstract Logix drew contributions from McLaughlin, Jan Hammer, and Mike Stern — a measure of the company he keeps.

Winners of a 2023 international prix competition and the 2024 ASCAP Herb Alpert Young Composer Award, this New York trio — saxophonist Abdias Armenteros, bassist Sebastian Rios, and drummer TJ Reddick — blend hard bop, hip-hop, and Afro-Cuban flavours. Armenteros holds a chair in the Lincoln Center Orchestra, while Rios studied under Ron Carter.

artist_name: Zahili Zamora Afro Cuban Jazz Trio
description: A winner of the DownBeat Award for Outstanding Performance and the Wayne Shorter Award, this Cuban-born pianist, composer and arranger brings her 2025 album Overcoming to life, recorded alongside luminaries including Sean Jones, Yosvany Terry and Pedrito Martínez.

Debut album Caged Bird on Mack Avenue Records in hand, this Washington D.C.-raised, Juilliard-trained vocalist took second place in the Sarah Vaughan International Vocal Competition before landing one of the year's most anticipated releases. Her voice draws from gospel and her Cameroonian heritage, arriving at Ronnie Scott's on 15 November.

Having made their BBC Proms debut in 2024 with two performances at the Royal Albert Hall, Fantasia Orchestra's principal players arrive at Ronnie's for an intimate programme spanning Shostakovich, Gershwin, Bernstein and Piazzolla. They are joined by award-winning pianist and arranger Harry Baker, whose commissions include the BBC Proms, the Philharmonia Orchestra and The King's Singers.

artist_name: Nathan Haines with guest vocalist Vanessa Freeman
description: New Zealand saxophonist Nathan Haines — whose album 5 A Day features Freeman alongside Jamiroquai and 4Hero collaborators — reunites with London vocalist Vanessa Freeman, who has performed alongside Herbie Hancock and Wayne Shorter. A long-running creative partnership returns to the Ronnie Scott's stage.

At Ronnie Scott's, his quintet draws on Vietnamese, Chinese and Andean musical traditions, performed on instruments gathered across travels through Asia, Europe and South America.

Led by pianist Renee Rosnes with trumpeter Ingrid Jensen, tenor saxophonist Nicole Glover, bassist Noriko Ueda and drummer Allison Miller. Three Blue Note albums to date; the latest, Arboresque, made the Guardian's top ten of 2025.

New York-born and Berlin-based, Sorvina brings her debut album Oh, the Places You'll Go to Ronnie Scott's, weaving neo-soul, gospel and hip-hop into poetic stories of identity, queerness, and joy. She won the Listen to Berlin platform's best artist award and received a nomination for the Reeperbahn Festival's Anchor Award.

MOBO-nominated singer-songwriter Natalie Williams brings her soulful command to Ronnie Scott's, the club where she has held a residency for 19 years. Joining her is pianist Jamie Safir, featured on the Decca solo piano album Alone Together — a pairing that promises an intimate evening of swing and soul.

South London singer-songwriter whose voice features on Theo Croker's Love Quantum, Ego Ella May brings her richly textured sound to Ronnie Scott's. Her 2026 album Good Intentions, released on Canvas Music, marks her most expansive collection yet.

Oakland-born pianist and vocalist who toured with Prince on the Musicology tour and performed at the 2004 Grammys alongside Beyoncé, she now leads the Trio whose debut album It's Time was released in 2018.

Copenhagen-born bassist Jasper Høiby, who built his reputation with the acclaimed piano trio Phronesis, brings his 3Elements project to Ronnie Scott's. Conversations of Hope, their third album on Edition Records, features a fresh trio lineup — a deliberate approach of assembling new collaborators for each release.

A Memphis-born saxophonist now based in New York, his sound is rooted in gospel, R&B and funk. He brings material from his release 1979 featuring pianist Julius Rodriguez, having also performed alongside Lauryn Hill and Olivia Dean.

Togo's Kossi Mawun brings his project Culte to Upstairs at Ronnie's — a drum-led exploration weaving West African sacred rhythms into contemporary improvisation. He made his European breakthrough supporting Makaya McCraven in France in autumn 2025, with pianist Joakim Amouzou and bassist David Kokodoko completing the trio.

Dakar-born bassist, vocalist and composer Alune Wade brings his 2025 ENJA/Yellow Bird album New African Orleans to Ronnie Scott's, tracing sonic connections between West African rhythms and New Orleans brass band music. A collaborator of Marcus Miller and Joe Zawinul, Wade bridges continents with a bass-driven sound rooted equally in Afrobeat and Senegalese tradition.

North London production duo NK-OK and Mr DM bring their rotating cast of guests to Ronnie Scott's stage. GRAMMY and MOBO nominated, the pair made their full-length debut with Motherland Journey on Blue Note Records, drawing collaborators including Tiana Major9, Ego Ella May, and Pip Millett.

His 2024 album Tales of the Facade explores themes of identity and community through richly layered compositions that move effortlessly between styles.

Honoured with the Order of Merit by the President of Portugal for his contribution to music, he brings a distinctly Pan-African voice to Ronnie Scott's stage on 22 November.

description: Korean pianist and composer Jisu Jung brings Baroque in Blue — her debut release on Korean independent label Wowsan Records — to Ronnie Scott's. Her quartet of piano, saxophone, viola and cello reimagines composers such as Bach through the groove and improvisational freedom of contemporary music.

He leads an international quartet whose music spans cinematic composition, improvisation and modern rock energy, moving between atmospheric passages and driving, high-energy moments.

description: New Orleans trombonist Delfeayo Marsalis brings his quintet to Ronnie Scott's, joined by tenor saxophonist Eric Alexander, known for his warm tone and bop-informed lyricism. Marsalis earned wide acclaim for his debut Pontius Pilate's Decision (1992), while Alexander has recorded prolifically for HighNote, including Temple of Olympic Zeus and Revival of the Fittest.

Double FM Award-winner Georgia Cécile has supported Gregory Porter on tour and performed with the BBC Concert Orchestra. This December, the Glasgow-born soul vocalist brings her festive show to Ronnie Scott's for a night of seasonal warmth and signature style.

Sydney-born singer-pianist whose latest EP Next Flight Home was recorded with Grammy Award-winning producer Cameron Craig, known for his work with Adele. She has supported Gregory Porter and Dionne Warwick, and her album Beautiful World earned five nominations at the Australian Songwriting Awards.

description: Trinidad-born Vanessa Haynes spent over 14 years as front woman of Incognito, cutting her teeth as a backing vocalist for Van Morrison and Chaka Khan.
